upsert.title: Fluorescence lifetime imaging to guide cancer surgery in dogs and cats
upsert.center: Ghent University Faculty of Veterinary Medicine
upsert.status: Recruiting — current Ghent University participation page invites dogs and cats scheduled for tumor surgery
upsert.contacts: Simone Janssen — simone.janssen@ugent.be; Prof. Hilde de Rooster — hilde.derooster@ugent.be; referrals: chirurgie.khd@ugent.be
upsert.funding: Project covers pathological assessment of the removed mass; Ghent states no additional costs compared with non-study surgical patients.
upsert.notes: Clinical study using intraoperative fluorescence lifetime imaging with indocyanine green to improve discrimination of tumor from non-tumor tissue and increase the chance of complete cancer removal during surgery. Dogs or cats with cancer already scheduled, or to be scheduled, for tumor resection may participate.
